conditional_argument.class: Ordinary non-null file DACL with one relevant allowed identity Q granting read plus DELETE but not WRITE_DAC; no matching deny, owner shortcut, privilege bypass, independent read ACE or required parent delete-child grant.
conditional_argument.actor_condition: Choose Q to be an ordinary enabled identity that survives the existing normal token filtering, so the current ambient read behavior actually applies. No administrator-only or disabled group grant is needed.
conditional_argument.normal_check: Q grants the stipulated read and DELETE. Removing Q from enabled identity matching loses the stipulated read as well.
conditional_argument.restricted_check_excluding_Q: A nonempty restricting list with no matching ACE cannot reproduce that read grant.
conditional_argument.restricted_check_including_Q: The same Q ACE can grant both read and DELETE in the second check; adding more nonmatching SIDs does not make Q conjunctive with them.
conditional_argument.no_per_SID_mask: The restricting list carries identities, not a separate rights mask for each identity. A new R SID without a matching object ACE supplies no read grant.
conditional_argument.empty_list_boundary: The current constructor already rejects empty capability input. Removing restrictions entirely would not supply outside-delete denial.
conditional_argument.preparation_boundary: Read permission does not establish WRITE_DAC. The stipulated non-owner, unprivileged caller cannot be assumed able to prepare a separate read ACE.
conditional_argument.kind: Source-and-documented-DACL reasoning only; no executed Windows fixture and no reconstructed native descriptor.
conditional_argument.conclusion: The existing flag/SID-only interface lacks a generic proof for preserving its ambient read behavior on arbitrary unprepared objects while denying deletion.
not_claimed: Necessity of exactly one R-SID design or one named preparation type
The conditional DACL is the actual complete DACL from Windows44

call_chain_conclusion.scope: These conclusions concern the sixteen bound bodies and inspected functions. They are not a whole-repository or Windows-platform absence proof.
call_chain_conclusion.reason: The raw inputs contain token/SID values, not resource coverage or a completed preparation receipt. The legacy paths construct that token before applying path ACL rules. The separate elevated helper uses shared identities, can skip builtin-readable roots, and may launch asynchronously or skip under a mutex; this does not establish the distinct completed authority proposed by the report.

native_claim_boundaries.prepared_and_three_ACL_direct_passes: Retained from root terminal receipt; no F0-F4 values or cleanup completion inferred.
native_claim_boundaries.broad_Result_err_mapping: The source maps each actual Result to err().map(kind); for that mapping alone None denotes successful return.
native_claim_boundaries.legacy_lossy_mapping: read_to_string(...).ok() and is_dir() discard error distinctions. None/false do not alone prove deletion and are not relabeled here.
native_claim_boundaries.repeated_output: No extra execution count is inferred from repeated printed context.
native_claim_boundaries.old_ACE_migration: Remains OPEN; no descriptor deletion or migration is proposed.

primary_sources_independently_opened.supports: WRITE_RESTRICTED applies restricting SIDs only to write evaluation; ordinary restriction needs both checks; restricting attributes are zero, and existing restriction lists intersect.
Enabled identities and restricting identities are checked separately; both must permit requested rights.
The direct DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION table requires READ_CONTROL to query and WRITE_DAC to set.
Changing security information has inheritance/propagation limits; the READ_CONTROL/WRITE_DAC distinction is sourced directly from the separate table above.
FILE_GENERIC_READ includes shared standard rights and SYNCHRONIZE; shared generic deny bits can interfere with reading.
